authority: Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe)
interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window or publication status.
sourcePolicy: IN-SPACe's official scheme documents and official portal are the controlling sources. Portal results and announcements are used for current-state detection only and do not prove an open application window.

records.sourceAnchor: Scheme document pages 2-7: purpose, eligible startup/MSE route, Indian ownership, matching investment, prior-support limit, grant ceiling, milestones, utilization, audit and application announcement; official portal current results/announcements
observations: The official scheme document describes seed capital for eligible startups and micro/small enterprises developing technology-led products or services in the commercial space sector.

The reviewed scheme document states up to INR 1 crore in grant support, released on milestones in three or more instalments; the exact amount and instalments are decided by an Experts Committee and are not applicant entitlements.

The earlier official document states an 80 percent Indian-shareholding condition, matching promoter/angel investment, a prior-government-support ceiling of INR 50 lakh subject to stated exclusions, three-year utilization and audited utilization obligations.

The current official portal shows Seed Fund results/use-case information and announcements, but the reviewed evidence does not establish that a new 2026 application window is open. The record therefore remains paused and non-actionable.
The benefit must remain a grant bucket separate from any later investment, prize, facility access, authorization or space-sector procurement opportunity.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current IN-SPACe announcement, closing date, operative application form and whether the Seed Fund is accepting new applications.
Reconcile the latest startup/MSE definition, Indian ownership, funding-round, matching-investment and prior-government-support rules against any current amendment.
Confirm space-sector scope, eligible costs, milestones, committee selection, instalment release, agreement, reporting, audit, recovery and IP conditions.
Confirm the authority mapping against the official IGOD/Department of Space source before treating the opportunity as authority-resolved or publication-ready.

records.sourceAnchor: SIDBI Venture Capital AVCF page: Category II AIF registration, fund manager, key investment criteria, mode of investment and contact/application route
observations: The primary operational source is the SIDBI Venture Capital Limited fund-manager page. The Playbook label must not be treated as a BIRAC programme.

AVCF is a SEBI-registered Category II AIF with IN-SPACe as key investor/anchor and SIDBI Venture Capital Limited as fund manager/sponsor. The fund page states that it seeks Indian space companies with TRL 4 or above.
The benefit is negotiated equity, convertible instruments and/or other permissible instruments in unlisted Indian space companies. It is not a grant, subsidy, loan or guaranteed Government payment.

The April 2026 Department of Space/PIB release reports an initial close with a committed corpus of INR 1,005 crore, while the August 2026 reply reports operation and selected startups. Fund corpus and selected-startup figures are not individual applicant benefits.

The public sources do not establish a universal ticket size, fixed deadline, automatic selection, valuation, dilution, governance or exit terms. The record therefore remains paused and non-actionable until current fund documents and diligence terms are reviewed.
reviewFollowUps: Verify the current SIDBI Venture Capital application/contact route, fund availability, operative form and latest fund documents.
Confirm Indian company, unlisted status, space-sector scope, TRL evidence and any additional financial, ownership, legal or commercial conditions.
Review the Private Placement Memorandum, investment instruments, ticket-size range, valuation, dilution, governance, fees, confidentiality, reporting, exit and committee process.
Confirm the IN-SPACe/Department of Space authority mapping against the official IGOD/Department of Space source before publication.

publicationGuard.reason: Official IN-SPACe documents support a structured seed-fund draft, but the current call, authority mapping, amendments and applicant-specific conditions remain unresolved. The record stays paused and human-review pending.
